ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism Act 2021 (AMLCFTA) and Business Corporations Act (MJ 21 MIRC Ch. 2) as amended, supplemented by the Registrar of Corporations Rules and the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) Beneficial Ownership Regulations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed registered agent within the Marshall Islands
Incorporator and notary public in the jurisdiction of execution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors (or intended directors) and notary public

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing government authority and notary public

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the UN Consolidated List, OFAC SDN, UK Sanctions List, and the RMI FIU National Sanctions List. Enhanced due diligence applies to politically exposed persons (PEPs), their family members, and close associates. All information is verified through independent sources and continuous transaction monitoring per the AMLCFTA 2021.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: RMI Corporate Registry Online Portal (Companies Registry Division, Ministry of Commerce and Industry)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names shall be registered in English (Latin script) only under section 7(1) of the Business Corporations Act. Names with diacritics, non-Latin script, or foreign characters are not accepted unless transliterated into roman characters. A complete English translation is required for any non-English words. All submitted names must be distinguishable and not contain prohibited tokens.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file a written appeal with the Registrar within 14 days, stating the grounds for reconsideration. The Registrar must issue a decision within 21 days. An adverse determination may be further appealed to the High Court of the Marshall Islands for judicial review under the Civil Procedure Rules, with no filing fee waiver available.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible solely as a service-of-process address, provided that the corporation maintains a licensed registered agent with a physical location in Majuro or Ebeye. A virtual office cannot replace the statutory registered office. Industry practice accepts a virtual address for non-resident corporations, but a statutory physical address is mandatory.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low — below 5% annualized for an inactive non-resident specialty tea salon with no local premises; moderate (10-20%) if the corporation later operates a physical tea salon within the Marshall Islands or triggers FIU reporting obligations. Unannounced inspections are authorized under the AMLCFTA and may occur upon filing of suspicious activity reports or upon material changes in beneficial ownership.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Associations Law of the Republic of the Marshall Islands, Title 14 – Business Corporations Act (BCA), ss. 43-47 (Articles of Incorporation), ss. 58-61 (Registered Office and Agent), ss. 75-86 (Directors, Bylaws and Organization Meetings)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Business Registry Division, Ministry of Resources and Development, Republic of the Marshall Islands, Majuro
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation on the official Business Corporations Act registry form
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; BCA requires at least one issued share; the subscription price is fixed by the board in US Dollars and no escrow account is mandated
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: that the Corporation hereby subscribes to and accepts the 1,000 authorized common shares at $1.00 par value per share, and the Secretary is directed to issue share certificates upon payment. FURTHER RESOLVED: that the registered office of the Corporation be fixed at the office of the Licensed Registered Agent, Republic of the Marshall Islands, and the agent is confirmed as statutory agent for service of process. FURTHER RESOLVED: that the directors appoint the President, Secretary, and Treasurer to hold office at the pleasure of the Board; each officer is authorized to open bank accounts, execute leases, negotiate vendor contracts, and bind the Corporation in the ordinary course of its specialty tea salon business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Name Reservation Unit, Business Registry Division, Ministry of Resources and Development, Majuro
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a licensed registered agent to file the Name Reservation Application for a proposed name ending in 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Limited' or an approved abbreviation; the declaration must state the corporate purpose as a specialty tea salon and lounge service under ISIC 5630.
required_dossiers: Statement of Corporate Purpose referencing ISIC 5630
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as confusingly similar, submit an administrative clarification with two alternative names; a resubmission within 5 business days is processed without additional registry review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Filing of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Business Registry Division, Ministry of Resources and Development, Majuro
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the Articles of Incorporation before a notary public and lodge the instrument with the Registrar through the licensed registered agent; specify authorized capital, number of directors, and the Majuro registered office address; remit the USD 150 statutory fee.
required_dossiers: Consent to Act of Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: On registry query, file a corrective amendment under BCA s. 57 within 21 days; clerical errors are cured by a signed correction certificate without additional state fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Registered Agent, Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt the agent's physical office address as the statutory registered office; the agent files the Registered Office Declaration and maintains the corporate minute book, share ledger, and company seal for inspection by the Registrar on demand.
required_dossiers: Corporate Minute Book and Share Register Set-Up
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the appointed agent declines service, appoint a substitute licensed agent and file a Change of Registered Agent notice within 7 days to preserve statutory continuity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Organization, Share Issuance, and Officer Appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Subscriber and Board of Directors acting through the Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the organization meeting of the incorporator to adopt bylaws and elect directors; the board then adopts the First Board Resolution authorizing subscription shares, confirming the registered office, and appointing the President, Secretary, and Treasurer; execute stock certificates and lodge minutes in the corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution or unanimous written consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If quorum fails, circulate a unanimous written consent in lieu of a meeting under BCA s. 86; defective minutes are ratified by a subsequent board resolution within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registry Certification and Certificate of Good Standing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Business Registry Division, Ministry of Resources and Development, Majuro
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon registration completion, obtain the Certificate of Incorporation, certified bylaws, and Certificate of Good Standing; verify the legal name, registered office, directors, and authorized capital against the registry docket before commencing physical salon operations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry certificate contains inaccurate data, file a written rectification request with supporting attested documents; the Registrar issues an amended certificate within 5 business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Business License Enforcement Office, Ministry of Finance, Republic of the Marshall Islands, in coordination with the Ministry of Resources and Development
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Domestic Business License for Food and Beverage Service under the Business License Act 2001, including retail specialty tea preparation and lounge service

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI EPA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category R (Registration) - Non-major Food and Beverage Service Screening; full EIA Report not required for premises under 200 m² connected to municipal wastewater
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: BOD not exceeding 50 mg/L, TSS not exceeding 50 mg/L, pH 6.0-9.0; no process water discharge into storm drains; installation of a grease trap; fugitive VOC emissions below 0.5% threshold; solid waste segregation and licensed hauler per RMI Solid Waste Regulations 1989

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Majuro Fire and Rescue Services fire clearance with occupancy load certificate (maximum 80 patrons), commercial kitchen suppression system inspection, and emergency exit verification; Ministry of Health public health sanitation clearance for food contact surfaces; building structural load inspection and Certificate of Occupancy from the Majuro Atoll Local Government.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance, Treasury and Foreign Investment, Marshall Islands Revenue and Customs Office (official portal: rmi-government.org)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The Marshall Islands imposes no income tax, VAT, GST, or sales tax; no general statutory TIN or VAT ID exists. A foreign-owned non-resident Business Corporation (BC) must obtain: (1) a Foreign Investment Business License (FIBL) from the Foreign Investment Advisor's Office under the Foreign Investment Business Act 1996, if engaging in licensed foreign-investment activity; (2) a Certificate of Incorporation from the Registrar of Corporations under the Business Corporations Act 1990; (3) an Employer Registration Number from the Marshall Islands Social Security Administration if any Marshall Islands employees are engaged, triggering monthly social security contributions; and (4) a Customs Importer Code from the Marshall Islands Revenue and Customs Office for any import of goods. Procedure: file the FIBL application with a business plan and evidence of capital, pay the statutory registration fees (approximately USD 250–750), and receive the certificates; no income-tax file number is issued or required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None under Marshall Islands domestic law: the Business Corporations Act 1990 contains no check-the-box or US-style elective entity classification regime. A non-resident Business Corporation is automatically treated as an offshore, non-taxable entity for RMI tax purposes. If a US person owns the BC, a US federal check-the-box election (IRS Form 8832) may independently apply for US tax classification; hybrid mismatch elections under OECD BEPS Action 2 are not recognized by RMI domestic statute.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT/GST/Sales Tax - Customs Import Duty and Ad Valorem Tariff Regime Only
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No VAT/GST registration threshold exists because no VAT/GST regime is in force. Customs importer registration is mandatory for any person or entity importing goods into the Marshall Islands regardless of value. Import duties are levied under the Customs Act 1990 and the Marshall Islands Tariff Schedule, generally 5%-10% ad valorem, with higher specific rates for fuel, alcohol, and tobacco.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None. The Marshall Islands does not operate a real-time electronic invoicing, fiscal clearance, API, or digital stamping regime. Commercial invoices require no tax-authority clearance. Customs clearance for imported goods is processed through the ASYCUDA World computerized customs declaration system; domestic and export invoices are paper-based or ordinary electronic invoices without fiscal validation or digital stamping.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable; with no VAT/GST regime in force there is no output tax to zero-rate and no VAT refund mechanism. Export sales of goods and offshore services from the Marshall Islands are entirely outside the scope of any indirect tax, and no export duty is imposed. Exporters of goods must file a customs export declaration for statistical and control purposes.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Certificate of Origin (where preferential tariff treatment is claimed)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: VAT zero-rating fraud is impossible in the absence of VAT. False customs declarations, including undervaluation, misdescription of goods, or unlicensed exportation, are prosecuted under the Customs Act 1990 and the RMI Criminal Code, with fines up to US$25,000, forfeiture of goods, and imprisonment up to five years. Retrospective customs reassessment is available for up to five years from the date of declaration; no VAT clawback regime exists.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: No domestic central bank; the Republic of the Marshall Islands Ministry of Finance and the Banking Commissioner exercise prudential banking supervision. The United States Federal Reserve serves as the de facto monetary authority because the U.S. dollar is the sole legal tender.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Marshall Islands maintains a fully dollarized, open financial system with no exchange-control restrictions. Both current-account and capital-account transactions are freely convertible into and out of U.S. dollars. Profit remittance, dividend distribution, and capital repatriation face no statutory conversion hurdles; however, banking institutions may apply internal due-diligence requirements and are bound by U.S. OFAC sanctions screening and anti-money-laundering protocols.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. As a dollarized economy with no foreign-exchange legislation, the Marshall Islands imposes no surrender obligation for export proceeds, no statutory conversion ratio, and no timeline for repatriation. Exporters may lawfully retain U.S. dollar receipts in domestic or offshore accounts, subject only to normal anti-money-laundering recordkeeping.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to Medium. Offshore digital EMI providers can supply U.S. dollar settlement, virtual account numbers, and card-acquiring services without being licensed as deposit-taking banks in the Marshall Islands. Legal constraint: the RMI Banking Act requires a banking license for deposit-taking, but a money-service business may operate under a money-transmitter authorization. For a low-risk specialty tea salon, a foreign EMI is viable only if it can support merchant card acquiring, SWIFT inbound wires, and outward USD payments; however, most EMIs impose restrictive OFAC/KYC policies and may require an RMI legal opinion confirming that the business does not constitute unauthorized banking activity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally mandatory. Bank of Marshall Islands requires at least one director and the authorized signatory to appear in person at a Majuro or Ebeye branch for the initial KYC interview. Bank of Guam likewise requires in-branch identity verification; remote opening is not a standard procedure. Video-conference KYC may supplement but cannot replace physical inspection of original documents. Acceptable documents include notarized passports, corporate registration certificate, articles of incorporation, certificate of good standing, board resolutions, and source-of-funds statements for every 10% beneficial owner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: International business corporation with non-resident directors and nominee shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the Marshall Islands corporate registry certificate, continuous good-standing certificate, audited or compiled financial statements, full beneficial-ownership schedule, notarized passport copies of all directors and ultimate beneficial owners, and a board resolution approving the account and its intended transactional profile.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inability to demonstrate lawful source of initial capital funding
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Three months of shareholder bank statements, sale and purchase agreements, inheritance and tax records, employment income letters, audited financial statements of the contributing entity, and a sworn affidavit of lawful source of funds and wealth.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear commercial purpose inconsistent with the stated ISIC 5630 specialty tea salon activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan, projected cash-flow statement, premises lease agreement, supplier contracts for tea and ceramic ware, product catalogue and price list, staff employment records, and municipal business license or interim license application confirmation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or high-risk jurisdiction nexus in transaction counterparties or funding chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: OFAC-compliant transaction flowcharts, correspondence letters from counsel confirming no sanctioned party involvement, enhanced due-diligence questionnaires, and the bank's internal compliance form documenting chain-of-funds and chain-of-custody for all counterparty relationships.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant US-dollar wire transfers via the bank's correspondent network, typically through U.S. clearing banks using ABA routing and SWIFT MT103 messages. The wire memo must reference the statutory purpose code 'Capital Contribution / Equity Injection' and include the corporate name, account number, invoice or board-resolution reference, and source-of-funds narrative. Bank of Marshall Islands will require a certified board resolution, a subscription agreement, a completed source-of-funds form, and OFAC-compatible proof of identity of the remitting shareholder. No currency conversion is required because the Marshall Islands uses USD as legal tender.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Payments for imported loose-leaf tea and cultural ceramic wares are cleared by SWIFT MT103 credit transfers, with commercial letters of credit used where supplier confidence requires a documentary credit. For domestic operating disbursements, the bank offers USD clearing via the local clearing system, branch-initiated cashier's cheques, and ACH or wire transfer to service providers. The bank may require underlying trade documents, including commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading/air waybill, and customs declaration, before releasing funds for cross-border supplier payments.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Offshore USD/EUR and USD/CNH deliverable forwards

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Return and Franchise Tax (consolidated government filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands (Office of the Attorney General)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due on the anniversary of the date of incorporation; eligible for a 30-day grace period before late fees accrue
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% monthly late penalty (capped at 100%); after 60 days past due the Registrar may administratively strike off the corporation; reinstatement requires payment of all arrears and penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent and Registered Office Annual Renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed Marshall Islands Registered Agent (agent of record with the Registrar)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the incorporation anniversary (contractual renewal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Lapse of registered agent or office for more than 30 days is a statutory ground for involuntary dissolution by the Registrar.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered Agent (records subject to inspection by the Registrar of Corporations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the incorporation anniversary; refreshed within 30 days of any share transfer, change of control, or ownership-structure modification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to confirm or knowingly filing false UBO data is an offense punishable by fine of up to USD 10,000 and possible administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Directory and Capital Change Notification (director, officer, or share capital amendments)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered Agent, reflected in the next Annual Corporate Return filed with the Registrar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of any corporate change occurring during the year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Misstatements in the annual return constitute a misdemeanor; liable to a fine and, for persistent default, deregistration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory independent audit is required for a non-resident Business Corporation under the Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act. An audit becomes compulsory only if the corporation is listed on a recognized stock exchange, is engaged in regulated banking or insurance activity, or the board voluntarily resolves to obtain audited financial statements. A non-resident specialty tea salon with no physical presence or taxable income in the Marshall Islands does not meet any compulsory audit threshold.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: The Marshall Islands has no domestically prescribed GAAP for tax-exempt non-resident corporations. Financial statements are customarily prepared in accordance with IFRS or US GAAP for banking, registered-agent due diligence, and internal governance purposes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The corporation must maintain a beneficial ownership register at the office of its registered agent identifying each individual who ultimately owns or controls 25% or more of the shares or voting power. An annual confirmation is executed by a director or officer verifying the accuracy of the register; any shareholding transfer requires the register to be updated and re-confirmed within 30 days. The registered agent must report apparent non-compliance or suspicious nominee arrangements to the Registrar of Corporations.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not applicable (no statutory audit); voluntary audit USD 4,000 - USD 8,000 per engagement

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Zero-tax jurisdiction for a Non-Resident Domestic Business Corporation (BC). The Marshall Islands Income Tax Act imposes no corporate income tax, no capital gains tax, no branch profits tax, and no estate or gift tax on a BC that has no Marshall Islands source income and no place of business within the Republic other than its registered office. The sole recurring fiscal charge is the annual franchise tax based on the number of authorized shares, ranging from USD 100 to USD 2,500, plus the annual report filing fee. No additional statutory tax holiday exists because the headline rate is already nil; the Non-Resident Domestic Corporation election is the operative tax exemption mechanism.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form AR-1, the Annual Report and Franchise Tax Statement, required under Section 59 of the Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act 1990 (as amended). Filed electronically through the Marshall Islands Online System (MIOS) or the Registrar of Corporations e-Registry, in practice submitted exclusively by the licensed Registered Agent. No corporate income tax return is filed in the Marshall Islands because a Non-Resident Domestic BC is wholly exempt from the Income Tax Act.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due on or before the last day of the anniversary month of incorporation. A BC incorporated on 15 March, for example, must file by 31 March of each year. The entity's adopted fiscal year-end is irrelevant to this deadline. No extension is available for non-resident entities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Corporate Name and Registration Number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exact legal name as shown on the Certificate of Incorporation, followed by the unique BC registration number assigned by the Registrar of Corporations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the English legal name only. No foreign tax identification number is required or requested at this stage for a non-resident BC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Registered Agent Name and Address
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name and physical address of the licensed Marshall Islands registered agent holding authority to act for the BC under the Business Corporations Act.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident BC cannot self-represent. The registered agent is the statutory service address, receives all official notices, and submits the annual report on behalf of the entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Physical street address of the registered office in the Marshall Islands, ordinarily the registered agent's premises in Majuro or Ebeye. A P.O. Box alone is insufficient.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident BC, this is typically the registered agent's office address. No local operational premises, staff, or lease must be disclosed here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full legal names and residential addresses of all directors and officers in office as of the filing date. Changes during the year must be reflected.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign residential addresses are accepted without restriction. Nominee directors must be identified as nominees, and the appointing beneficial owner must be disclosed to the registered agent for AML record-keeping and CRS purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Authorized Shares and Par Value
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Number of authorized shares, par value per share (or no-par designation), and total authorized capital expressed in USD. This data determines the franchise tax bracket.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Authorized share count must match the incorporation filing. Authorizing fewer than 50,000 shares keeps the annual franchise tax at the USD 100 minimum; deliberate under-capitalization to minimize tax is permissible under the Act but invites anti-abuse scrutiny by foreign revenue authorities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sliding-scale annual franchise tax computed on the number of authorized shares: USD 100 for up to 50,000 shares; USD 200 up to 100,000; USD 300 up to 250,000; USD 500 up to 500,000; USD 750 up to 1,000,000; USD 1,000 up to 5,000,000; USD 1,500 up to 50,000,000; USD 2,500 for more than 50,000,000 shares.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payable in USD, typically remitted by the registered agent. No revenue, turnover, profit, or balance sheet disclosure is required from a non-resident BC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sworn declaration confirming the BC (i) has no office or place of business in the Republic except the registered office, (ii) derives no income from sources within the Marshall Islands, and (iii) is not licensed to carry on business locally. This declaration is the operative trigger for Income Tax Act exemption.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The declaration is signed by a director or the registered agent under penalty of perjury. A false declaration is a criminal offense and grounds for involuntary dissolution. For the Specialty Tea Salon Lounge, it also files a foreign substance questionnaire where the operating jurisdiction imposes CFC or economic substance obligations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmation that no prior-year franchise tax, penalties, or annual reports are outstanding and that the BC is entitled to a Certificate of Good Standing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Request the Certificate of Good Standing simultaneously; it is required for foreign bank account opening, merchant POS processing agreements, and foreign tax authority substance reviews.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form AR-1 attracts a flat penalty of USD 200 imposed by the Registrar. Unpaid franchise tax accrues a 10% per-month surcharge, or the USD 200 flat penalty, whichever is greater. Failure to file and pay for two consecutive years triggers administrative dissolution by the Registrar without a court order. A dissolved BC loses all legal standing to sue or defend in Marshall Islands courts, its assets escheat for administration of creditors' claims, and reinstatement requires a High Court petition plus payment of all arrears, surcharges, and reinstatement fees.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Not applicable in substance. The Marshall Islands maintains no comprehensive double taxation agreement; its network consists principally of Tax Information Exchange Agreements and the special taxation arrangement with the United States under the Compact of Free Association. Because the statutory dividend withholding rate is 0%, no DTA relief, tax residence certificate, or reduced-rate application is required for outbound dividends, and no Marshall Islands tax authority filing exists for such payments. Where a foreign shareholder's home jurisdiction taxes the dividend, relief is obtained exclusively in that foreign jurisdiction through foreign tax credit, participation exemption, or applicable treaty provisions; the Marshall Islands payer issues no withholding certificate. In the hypothetical event of a future comprehensive DTA, the standard protocol would be: (1) the shareholder obtains a Certificate of Residence (TRC) from its home tax authority; (2) lodges it with the paying agent before the dividend record date; (3) the agent retains the TRC and dividend register for six years; and (4) any reduced rate is applied at source.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on cross-border IP royalties: 0%. Statutory withholding on debt interest: 0%. The Marshall Islands does not impose a gross-basis final withholding regime on non-resident BCs for outbound interest, royalties, license fees, or management fees. Treaty rates are not applicable because no comprehensive double taxation convention is in force. Foreign substance jurisdictions, however, may recharacterize excessive or undocumented royalty and interest flows under their own transfer pricing and earnings-stripping rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No Marshall Islands domestic transfer-pricing documentation threshold is codified. Practical compliance benchmark: USD 1,000,000. Where the BC engages in cross-border related-party transactions exceeding USD 1,000,000 in aggregate annual value, a Local File commensurate with the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines (BEPS Action 13) should be prepared and retained to preserve the zero-tax position against foreign recharacterization. The Marshall Islands imposes no Country-by-Country Reporting obligation on the BC itself; however, if the BC belongs to an MNE group above EUR 750 million consolidated revenue, it must supply financial and ownership data to the ultimate parent entity for CbC reporting purposes.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Marshall Islands has not enacted a formal Economic Substance Regulations regime in the BVI or Cayman model, and the OECD Forum on Harmful Tax Practices accepts its zero-tax treatment of non-resident BCs without a local substance test. Nevertheless, economic substance is the critical anti-abuse benchmark enforced by foreign revenue authorities. For an ISIC 5630 Specialty Tea Salon Lounge, substance is demonstrated by: (1) a physical licensed tea salon, retail counter, and cultural ceramic venue in the operating market; (2) local employees, payroll records, and management decisions in that market; (3) point-of-sale and banking infrastructure in the operating country; and (4) accounting records maintained at the registered agent or a recognized record-keeping location. If the BC operates as a pure invoicing or brand-holding shell without these indicia, foreign tax courts may recharacterize it as having a permanent establishment or place of effective management at the operating site, imposing local corporate income tax, VAT, and payroll liabilities retroactively. CRS and FATCA reporting obligations remain independently applicable to the beneficial owners.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Falsely claiming Non-Resident Domestic Corporation status while the BC's place of effective management, staff, sales operations, or material assets are de facto located in a foreign taxing jurisdiction; or using the BC as an invoice-stripping conduit that invoices specialty tea and ceramic sales at inflated margins to divert profit away from the operating jurisdiction without arm's-length intercompany agreements, substance, or supporting documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: In the foreign operating jurisdiction: recharacterization of the BC as tax-resident, assessment of back corporate income tax, VAT, payroll taxes, interest, and civil penalties of up to 200% of the underpaid tax. In the Marshall Islands: strike-off and administrative dissolution for a false Box 7 declaration, judicial dissolution petition by the Attorney General under the Business Corporations Act, and forfeiture of the corporate franchise. The Republic cooperates with foreign revenue authorities through Tax Information Exchange Agreements and mutual legal assistance treaties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who sign the false non-resident declaration face perjury prosecution under the Marshall Islands Criminal Code and personal liability for foreign unpaid taxes where the corporate veil is pierced for fraud. Cross-border consequences include civil restitution orders in the operating jurisdiction, international travel bans, asset freezes, and extradition requests; imprisonment of up to 10 years may attach under the revenue statutes of the prosecuting jurisdiction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance / Nominee Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining nominee directors who exercise no authority or knowledge, operating from a bare registered-agent address with no local books and records, and presenting the BC to banks, merchants, landlords, or licensors as an active specialty tea operator while it has zero operational footprint, no payroll, and no Board minutes or management accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Registrar may administratively dissolve the BC for failure to maintain records or for false attestations; monetary penalties up to USD 25,000 may be imposed for knowingly false filings under the Business Corporations Act; the BC loses legal standing to sue or defend; and foreign revenue and banking authorities will aggregate the BC's assets and flows with the beneficial owner's direct income, imposing back taxes and anti-avoidance penalties under GAAR, CFC, and substance-over-form doctrines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors face civil restitution orders and disqualification from holding directorships for up to 15 years. Beneficial owners are exposed to fraudulent-trading liability when the BC is insolvent and to criminal prosecution for using the shell to evade licensing, immigration, tax, or creditor claims. Asset seizure, personal bankruptcy proceedings, and enforcement of foreign civil judgments against personal assets follow in practice.
